name: Mod style

card.summary: The sharp, tailored 1960s British subculture look of slim suits, skinny ties, crisp shirts and neat hair, a template for a polished, put-together appearance.
card.aka: mod fashion; modernist style; mod revival
card.note: A clothing and grooming style; tailoring is the main cost.

quick.overview:
Mod style comes from the late-1950s London subculture whose members, called modernists, wore sharp, tailor-made clothes inspired by Italian and French fashion. For someone trying to look better, it offers a polished, slim and neat look built from fitted suits, knitwear and tidy grooming.

The look spread across Britain, was revived in the late 1970s after the film Quadrophenia, and still influences menswear, including three-button suits and Chelsea boots.
quick.how: Male mod dress, as described by Wikipedia, centred on suits with narrow lapels (sometimes in mohair), skinny ties, button-down shirts, crew- or V-neck jumpers, and footwear such as Chelsea boots, loafers and desert boots, with hair styled after French New Wave actors. Parkas were worn over the outfit when riding scooters. Casual or hard-mod variants used Fred Perry polos, Sta-Prest trousers, braces and Dr. Martens boots.
quick.risks: Clothing carries little physical risk. Tailor-made suits are costly and fit depends on body proportions. Historically the subculture is also associated with amphetamine use and with clashes with rockers in 1964.

lead: Mod style is the fashion associated with the mod subculture that began in late-1950s London and spread across Great Britain. The name comes from 'modernist', a term used for modern jazz fans in the 1950s. Early mods were mostly working-class young men who took style cues from French and Italian art films and magazines. [1]

For appearance, the style emphasises sharp tailoring, slim lines and careful grooming. Male mods wore tailor-made suits with narrow lapels, skinny ties, button-down shirts and wool or cashmere jumpers, with hairstyles copied from French New Wave actors. [1]
The look was revived in the late 1970s, partly inspired by the 1979 film Quadrophenia and bands such as The Jam, and continues to influence menswear today. [1]

chain: Slim, fitted tailoring and clean lines
angle.text: The mod look gives a ready template for dressing sharply: fitted suits, narrow ties, button-down shirts, knitwear and tidy hair. Because it relies on proportion and fit, it presents the body in a neat, slim silhouette.

paras: Male mods wore tailor-made suits with narrow lapels, sometimes in mohair, with skinny ties, button-down shirts and crew- or V-neck wool or cashmere jumpers. Footwear included Chelsea or Beatle boots, loafers, Clarks desert boots and bowling shoes. The American Ivy League collegiate look was a major influence. [1]

Early mods sometimes wore ready-made clothes; later they customised items such as jackets, sometimes with pop-art versions of the Union Flag or RAF roundel. Some male mods wore eye shadow, eyeliner or lipstick. [1]

Many female mods were androgynous, with short hair, men's trousers or shirts, flat shoes, minimal makeup and false eyelashes. Hard mods favoured Fred Perry and Ben Sherman shirts, Sta-Prest trousers, braces, Dr. Martens boots and close-cropped hair. [1]

Mods rode Vespa or Lambretta scooters, customised with extra mirrors, racks, crash bars and chrome. Many wore ex-military parkas to keep their clothes clean while riding. Music included modern jazz, American R&B and soul and Jamaican ska, with venues such as the Flamingo and the Marquee in London. Bands with mod followings included The Who, Small Faces and The Kinks. [1]

By about 1963 the scene had its familiar symbols of scooters, amphetamines and R&B. Clashes with rockers peaked in 1964 at seaside towns including Margate and Brighton, which sociologist Stanley Cohen analysed in Folk Devils and Moral Panics. [1]

From about 1965 to 1966 Swinging London, with boutiques on Carnaby Street, brought the style into mainstream fashion, and by 1966 mod was fading as a dandy scene grew. In the late 1960s hard mods evolved into skinheads, and mod declined in the early 1970s. [1]

The late-1970s British revival drew thousands to scooter rallies, and an early-1980s North American revival followed in Southern California. Britpop bands such as Oasis and Blur in the 1990s showed mod influence, and Paul Weller is called the ModFather. [1]
Mod-inspired items such as three-button suits and Chelsea boots remain in fashion. [1]

timeline.event: Mod emerges in London among modern jazz fans and spreads across Britain. [1]
